rejected.title: Transport, technology and access
card: Access means how easily people can reach services and activities, such as a doctor, a school, a job or a sports club.
Transport
Roads, buses, trains and trams carry people to places. Where these are missing, unreliable or far apart, getting to services takes more time and effort.
Technology
The internet lets people use some services without travelling, such as online lessons or video calls with a doctor. It only helps where a connection is available and works well.
Good transport and technology make it easier to reach services and activities, so a place is usually easier to live in. Without them, a place can be harder to live in.
rejected.remember: Good roads, public transport and internet can make it easier to reach what people need.

a.q: Why can a good internet connection make a place easier to live in?
opts: People can reach services like lessons from home
It brings hospitals and shops closer to homes
It makes buses and trains run more often
It makes travelling by road quicker and safer
a.why: The internet lets people use some services without travelling, such as online lessons or video calls with a doctor. It does not move hospitals or shops, and it does not change buses, trains or roads. Those are part of transport, not technology.
a.clue: Think about what people can do without leaving home.

b.q: Ben lives on a farm in the Northern Territory. The nearest bus stop is a long drive away and his internet often drops out. What is the likely effect on his access to services?
opts: It is harder for him to reach services and activities
It is easier for him to reach services and activities
It makes no difference to how he reaches services
It means he needs fewer services than other people
b.why: Without nearby public transport or a reliable internet connection, Ben has fewer ways to reach services, so his place can be harder to live in. Having poor access does not mean he needs fewer services. It means getting to them takes more time and effort.
b.clue: Ask what ways Ben has to reach a service, in person or online.

draft.title: Transport, technology and access
card: Access means how easily people can reach services and activities, such as a doctor, a school, a job or a sports club.
Transport
Roads, buses, trains and trams carry people to places. Where these are missing, unreliable or far apart, getting to services takes more time and effort.
Technology
The internet lets people use some services without travelling, such as online lessons or video calls with a doctor. It only helps where a connection is available and works well.
Good transport and technology make it easier to reach services and activities, so a place is usually easier to live in. Without them, a place can be harder to live in.
draft.remember: Roads, public transport and the internet decide how easily people reach what they need.

a.q: Why does a good internet connection make a place easier to live in?
opts: People can use some services without travelling
People no longer need any roads or public transport
Services move closer to every home in the area
Everyone in the place can reach every service in person
a.why: The internet lets people do some things from home, such as online lessons or video calls with a doctor. It does not replace every service or remove the need for roads, so the option about not needing transport is wrong.
a.clue: Think about what people can do without leaving home.

b.q: Ben lives on a farm in the Northern Territory. The nearest bus stop is a long drive away and his internet often drops out. What is the likely effect on his access to services?
opts: It is harder for him to reach services and activities
It is easier for him to reach services and activities
It makes no difference to how he reaches services
It means he does not need any services
b.why: Without nearby public transport or a reliable internet connection, Ben has fewer ways to reach services. This makes the place harder to live in. Having no easy access does not mean he needs fewer services.
b.clue: Ask what ways Ben has to reach a service, in person or online.

a.best: People can use some services without travelling

b.best: It is harder for him to reach services and activities

problems.detail: "decide how easily people reach what they need" is stronger than the card, which says good transport and technology make a place "usually" easier to live in and that without them a place "can be" harder.

The right option is the only one with a qualifier ("some"). The three distractors all use absolutes ("every home", "everyone… every service", "no longer need any"), so a student could pick the answer without knowing the idea.
Why (b) says "This makes the place harder to live in" as a certainty, where the card says a place "can be" harder to live in.

check.summary: Both questions have one clear right answer. The remember line and why (b) overstate the card's "usually" and "can". In question a, the right option is the only one without an absolute, so it is easy to guess.
